title: Trim observability hotpath, add async envelope writer, and upgrade OpenTelemetry
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Reduce latency and CPU impact of telemetry hotpaths by introducing a lightweight async envelope writer for exported spans/metrics, trimming hotpath allocations, and upgrading the platform OpenTelemetry stack to a stable release. The work targets realtime inference hot paths inside the serving runtime and the telemetry forwarder that currently contributes to tail-latency spikes under high QPS.
background: We've observed 95th/99th percentile latency regressions correlated with telemetry flush spikes during large model-serving bursts. Root cause traces indicate allocations and lock contention in the sync span writer and exporter multiplexers (journal, protobuf encoding, exporter fanout). The current OTEL integration is pinned to an older SDK that blocks on exporter backpressure in some fast paths.
goals: Introduce an async, lock-free envelope writer that batches outgoing telemetry with bounded memory and backpressure semantics
Upgrade OpenTelemetry SDK and instrumentation to v1.14 (or the latest stable) and validate exporter compatibility
Move minimal serialization off the hotpath (defer protobuf marshalling to background workers)
Reduce per-span allocation and log context copies by 60% in the serving runtime
Ship a toggled rollout and observability checks so we can validate improvements and rollback quickly
tasks: Audit and map hotpath call sites that synchronously serialize or flush telemetry (trace, metric, log bridges)
Design async envelope writer API and bounded ring buffer layout for common carriers
Implement a background marshaller pool that reuses buffers and avoids per-span heap allocations
Integrate envelope writer into telemetry forwarder and runtime fastpath with feature flag gating
Upgrade OTEL SDK and replace deprecated hooks; run smoke tests across exporters (OTLP, Jaeger, Prometheus bridge)
Benchmark latency, CPU, and allocation profiles pre/post change under synthetic load
Rollout plan: internal canary -> staged regions -> full rollout with rollback guards
acceptance_criteria: P99 tail latency for inference requests shows no regression vs baseline; P95 improves by >=10% under the same workload
Heap allocations attributable to telemetry in the runtime decrease by >=60% on representative worker nodes
Export pipeline remains within quota: exporter retry/backoff behavior remains unchanged from API-level semantics
No increase in telemetry loss beyond acceptable baseline (<=1% packet loss under peak) during rollout
All existing dashboards and trace contexts (trace_id/span_id) preserved end-to-end and linkable in the console
design_decisions: Use an async envelope format (compact header + serialized payload) to allow the hotpath to write a fixed-size envelope reference rather than performing full protobuf marshalling
Prefer lock-free single-writer multiple-consumer ring buffer where possible; fallback to adaptive spin-wait for rare contention on small instances
Keep the OTEL upgrade and envelope writer feature-flagged so the control plane can toggle per-deployment during carveouts
Do not change the public trace/span schema; perform transformations only in the forwarder to maintain compatibility with existing dashboards
deploy_plan: Stage 0: Unit + integration tests in CI; run full e2e telemetry smoke tests on staging
Stage 1: Canary on 2 low-traffic clusters with feature flag enabled (48h)
Stage 2: Staged rollout with 10%/30%/60% increments (24h per step) monitoring P95/P99 and exporter queue depths
Stage 3: Full rollout if metrics stable for 72h
Add guardrails: automated rollback when P99 increases by >15% or exporter retry rates double
rollback_plan: Toggle feature flag off to revert to synchronous writer (fast path restore)
If feature-flag toggle fails, redeploy previous runtime binary pinned in the release manifest
Open incident and revert OTEL SDK upgrade via staged dependency pin in the forwarder image
risks: New background marshaller may increase memory usage if backpressure misconfigured
OTEL upgrade could change sampler hooks behavior; need careful validation to avoid sampling regressions
Race conditions in lock-free structures are hard to fully test; mitigations include targeted fuzzing and stress tests
Exporter compatibility issues (a downstream collector may not accept the new envelope format) — compatibility shim included
test_plan: Unit: ring buffer, marshaller pool, and envelope writer edge cases (wraparound, full/empty)
Integration: end-to-end traces from runtime -> forwarder -> OTLP collector -> console links
Load: generate sustained 10k RPS with mixed short/long traces to validate P95/P99 and memory usage
Chaos: inject exporter latency and temporary failures to validate backpressure and bounded queue behavior
monitoring_checks: P99 inference latency trend (compare rolling window to baseline)
Heap allocation rate from telemetry package (new metric) decreases by >=60%
Dropped telemetry count remains <=1% under peak
